components.html:
Below are 2 issues that have been reported. They are not typical of the quality of the machines, but ... mistakes happen in manufacturing.

Not every machine has this issue.
Inside the machine bed is a METAL holder that will control the "wings" of the mast.
If your mast sits high and twists inside the plastic holder, it needs to be positioned low enough so the "wings" of the mast sit IN THE SLOTS of the metal holder.
  • Main Bed: All needles are in "A" position (all the way back)
  • If Needle LEFT #10 does not align with the other needles
  • That ONE needle needs to be replaced with a shorter needle
    • That single needle can hit the bracket inside the machine that holds the tension mast. This is only an issue on select machines.

Use your PDF reader search feature to find terms and instruction in the PDF.
NOTE:To make the PDF searchable and keep the file size low, the images may be distorted

The printed manuals provided with the TH/TR 160 were "cobbled together" from bits and pieces of previous Brother manuals.
They are not as clear as we would expect them to be. This is the reason this course was created.

NOTES

1
Pages 13 and 14 of the ribber manual refer to "needle Stoppers", "Presser holders" and "extension racks". These accessories are not included with the TR-160 ribber.
2
Some machines are shipping with a sub take up spring on the yarn mast. Previous Brother manuals refer to this extra spring for 2 uses (both of which aren't applicable to this machine):
  1. Punch Lace | Thread Lace (this is not a possible with the TH-160 machine)
  2. Isolated Motif (this is helpful when automatic patterning - also not available on this machine)

components.html:
In working with the TH160 we discovered that the claw weights didn't match up with the spacing on the cast on comb.
In order to hang the weights cleanly on the cast on comb, we bent back 4 of the teeth.
Even if you use this weight to hang in your knitting, the remaining teeth will work as well as the original arrangement.

The 6mm gauge of this machine gives a lot of flexibility in the yarn we can use. It's your choice! you can choose a lightweight yarn and knit it at a very loose tension for a lightweight fabric. You can knit the same yarn at a tighter tension for a very different look. The fiber, color and texture of the yarn is up to you.
The only limit is the size of the needles. If the yarn is too thick and doesn't fit in the hooks of the needles, it can split and/or jam the machine.

components.html:
We can knit so much more than plain stockinette with this machine. With just a few carriage settings, quickly add texture and color.
This is a manual machine. There is no automatic needle selection (punchcard or electronics). Needles are positioned manually.
It is critical that you understand the 3 elements that create stitch patterns.
3 settings control stitch patterning:
1
Needle position
2
Change Lever
3
Cam Lever(s)
1
Needle position
Marked on the side of the needlebed A-B-D-E represent:
A Out of Work Position (Non-working Position |NWP) Unused Needles
B Working Position (WP) Needles lined up to knit in stockinette and most stitch patterns
D Middle Position(MP) (Pattern Position) Bring the needles from holding position into working and pattern work positions
E Holding Position (HP) The farthest position from "A" on the needlebed
2
Change Lever
The Change Lever controls the action of the needles for specific stitch types.
3
Cam Lever(s)
The Cam Levers are also called the hold levers
and control the action of needles in "E" position. Often used for short row shaping.

Explore the carriage settings.
Cast on and have some knitting on the needles.

sections.title:
Cam Levers:
  1. Set both cam levers to "H"
  2. Needles in A-B-D-E
  3. Pass the carriage
sections.bodyHtml:
• A - Needles do not knit (no matter what the carriage settings)
  • B - Needles Knit
  • D - Needles Knit
  • E - Needles do not knit

sections.title:
Cam Levers:
  1. Set both cam levers to "H"
  2. Opposite the carriage, place 10 needles in E
  3. Pass the carriage
sections.bodyHtml:
All needles EXCEPT the needles in hold position will knit.
This is the technique behind short row shaping/partial knitting.
  • A - Needles do not knit (no matter what the carriage settings)
  • B - Needles Knit
  • D - Needles Knit
  • E - Needles do not knit (hold | yarn passes over these needles)
Because the yarn passes over the needles in hold, this setting is also used for TUCK on this machine.

sections.title:
Change Lever:
  1. Change Lever to "PLAIN"
  2. Cam Levers to "N"
  3. Needles in A-B-D-E
sections.bodyHtml:
This is the setting for plain knitting (stockinette)
  • A - Needles do not knit (no matter what the carriage settings)
  • B - Needles Knit
  • D - Needles Knit
  • E - Needles Knit

sections.title:
Change Lever:
  1. Change Lever to "PART"
  2. Cam Levers to "N"
  3. Needles in B
sections.bodyHtml:
This is the setting for slip/skip and FREE PASS
  • A - Needles do not knit (no matter what the carriage settings)
  • B - Needles do not knit (slip/skip)
  • D - Needles Knit
  • E - Needles Knit

sections.title:
Change Lever:
  1. Change Lever to "INTAR"
  2. Cam Levers to "N"
  3. Needles in B
  4. NO YARN in the feeder
sections.bodyHtml:
All needles will be positioned to "D" with the latches open.
This is a specific setting to prepare for INTARSIA KNITTING . All 4 steps must be in place.

components.html:
Save your back, neck and shoulders
In these videos, you'll see me pushing the carriage with one hand. BAD!!!! I'm reaching around the camera.
When you are knitting use both hands and push and pull alternately to move the carriage.
Many knitters also adjust their knitting table so they can stand while knitting.

NOTE:
On this machine the ribber and main bed needles are the same.

For many more cast-on tips and techniques, visit:
the Knit it Now Classroom: Cast on Methods

Here is a fast way to create a closed, e-wrap cast on by using the knitting carriage.
This method is helpful if you want to avoid manually wrapping each needle.
Using the "slip" setting: Needles in "B" position don't knit
A single needle in "E" position (next to the carriage) will wrap.
  1. Set the cam to "slip"
  2. Carriage on the left, pull 1 needle to "E" Position
  3. Pass the carriage right (the yarn will wrap and the needle will return to "B" position)
  4. Pass the carriage left (the needle will not knit)
  5. repeat for the number of needles needed
  6. Hang a cast on comb
  7. Continue knitting

No sound

Tuck is a great way to add texture and interest to your knitting.
When knitting tuck, certain needles do not knit and the working yarn travels OVER the needles out of work.
  • Change the number of rows tucked
  • Change the needles selected
  • Change the number of rows between tucks
  • Put some needles out of work
  • Add color
  • Mix 'n match stitch patterns
Once you understand how tuck stitch is created on your machine, the sky's the limit!
3 settings control TUCK:
1
Needle position ("E")
2
Change Lever PLAIN
3
Cam Lever(s) "H" (hold/tuck)

For tuck inspiration, tips and techniques, visit:
the Knit it Now Classroom: Tuck Talk

Slip is a great way to add texture and interest to your knitting.
When knitting slip, certain needles do not knit and the working yarn travels UNDER the needles out of work.
  • Change the number of rows slipped
  • Change the needles selected
  • Change the number of rows between slip rows
  • Put some needles out of work
  • Add color
  • Mix 'n match stitch patterns
Once you understand how tuck stitch is created on your machine, the sky's the limit!
3 settings control SLIP:
1
Needle position ("D")
2
Change Lever PART
3
Cam Lever(s) "N" (normal)

For slip inspiration, tips and techniques, visit:
the Knit it Now Classroom: Slip Stitch
Check out the Knit it Now Stitch Library for Slip and Multi-Color Slip Stitch inspiration!

Since this machine has only 1 cam setting for slip (part) to work I-cord or circular knitting means flipping the cam lever from Part to Plain with every pass of the carrriage.
This can get tedious. Explore a work around, by putting needles into D or E position.

Also called "Picture Knitting", Intarsia is a technique that allows color changes in the middle of the row without having floats across the back of the knitting.
Once you understand how Intarsia is created on your machine, the sky's the limit!
3 settings control INTARSIA:
1
Needle position ("D")
2
Change Lever INTAR
3
Cam Lever(s) "N" (normal)

For intarsia inspiration, tips and techniques, visit:
the Knit it Now Classroom: Intarsia

Knit 2 strands of yarn together and let the machine position them so you view one color on one side of the knitting
and the 2nd color on the other side of the knitting.
  • When choosing the yarn for plaiting, remember both strands are knitting at the same time. The combined strands must fit in the hooks of the needles. This technique is best used with a thinner yarn than you would normally choose for this machine.

  • Key to plaiting is positioning the yarns correctly in the yarn feeder

Settings for Plaiting:
1
Needle position B-C-D
2
Change Lever PLAIN
3
Cam Lever(s) "N" (normal)

This machine does not have weaving brushes. But the beautiful technique of Knit Weave can be manually worked.
Weaving on the knitting machine can produce beautifully textured fabric. it's a fun way to use small amounts of novelty or luxury yarns on your machine knit projects.
Also possible are some interesting "lifted" techniques to add even more options to using the Knit Weave technique.
Practice dropping and raising the ribber. It's noisy and intimidating at first, but it's important that you get comfortable with this.

When using the ribber, position the mast so it's leaning toward you.
  • Look for the bend in the lower section of the mast
  • Turn it as shown in the video
  • Swivel the yarn guide to the back
  • Rotate the tension mast assembly

When working on the main bed only, reverse the setup so the mast is leaning away from you.
This is not critical, but the most important thing is that your yarn flows smoothly no matter how you set up the mast.

components.html: With English Rib, (Half-Fisherman Rib) one needlebed tucks every other row.
English Rib Carriage Settings: Tuck on the ribber to the RIGHT

Alternating tuck on each needlebed produces Fisherman Rib. Working this stitch pattern on this machine is a little different than other machines, so watch this video to make sure you understand this difference before trying this technique.

With the ribber, you can set your machine to knit in the round and eliminate seaming tubular pieces. Yes, there are some limitations, but this technique is very useful for a number of applications.
  • What about quickly knitting hats and caps without a seam?
  • Knit socks in the round
  • You can even knit the body of a plain garment to the armholes, then split the fronts and backs and knit them on the single bed, eliminating the side seams
Steps for Circular Knitting on the TH160
  1. Cast on as for full needle rib:
    • Ribber set to Half Pitch "H"
    • All needles in work
    • Zig Zag with Ravel cord - right to left (end with the carriage on the left)*
    • Hang the Cast On Comb and weights
    • Change to main yarn
  2. Row 1 (carriage on the left)
    • Main bed set to plain knitting
    • Ribber (Tuck lever "R" AND right Cam Lever "P-R")
    • Knit right (All needles on the main bed knit only)
  3. Row 2 (carriage on the right)
    • Main bed set to slip (part)
    • Ribber set to knit to the left (Tuck lever "R" AND left Cam Lever "N")
    • Knit Left (All needles on the ribber knit only)
Repeat these 2 rows alternating the main bed part button on every other row
Note that the only setting change is the main bed "part" button every other row. The ribber setting remains the same for the entire pattern

*Also note that this creates an open cast on. Other steps need to be taken to create a closed cast on and to bind off
